editorial:
Imagine being a proud dad who thinks his kids are all super successful, only to find out that life isn't exactly what it seems. You follow Matteo, a retired guy from Sicily who decides to travel across Italy to surprise his five children. He has spent years believing they are all doing great in their high-power jobs, but as he visits them one by one, you start to notice things aren't adding up. It is a slow-burn story that feels very human and relatable, focusing on the distance that can grow between parents and children even when they love each other.

The acting is really heartfelt and makes you feel the weight of the secrets being kept. While the pacing is a bit slow at times, the emotional payoff is totally worth it. You will probably find yourself thinking about your own family while watching. It is a great pick for a quiet Sunday night when you want something that actually makes you feel something.
endingExplained: You eventually find out the heartbreaking truth: none of Matteo's children are actually alive. They all passed away years ago. The people he visited were strangers or acquaintances who lied to him because they didn't want to break his heart. Matteo actually knew the truth the whole time. He just wanted to visit the people who had been kind enough to keep the lie going and give him a reason to keep living.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves emotional family stories and unexpected twists.
